what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours, 11 commits, five substantive, and the thesis got its answer: **the company has no inference advantage, and on this world it could not have one.** Both halves were proven this stretch and they corroborate rather than merely coexist. On all 478 renewals the world rolled -- 157 accounts, 2016-12-31 to 2025-06-06, an order of magnitude past the 25 the last reading rested on -- the belief's `discrimination_auc` is 0.5586 and the company's own logged estimate 0.5275, against an ORACLE CEILING of 0.8109 computed by grading the world's own `realized_churn_probability` by the identical statistic. The population is rankable; the company captures almost none of it. The inversion the last direction sent a tick to chase was n=4 and n=11 and it is gone: the buckets are monotone (0.899 / 0.916 / 0.936), the model has the DIRECTION of bill shock right (`sign_agrees_with_model: true`) and the DOSE wrong by 7.76x, with the level 2.63x too pessimistic. Then the third arm settled the money question the other way round from the flattering one: over the decade `flat_at_level` at the value arm's own realised median beats the control by £8,454.96 where `value_based` beats it by £7,065.86, so **the level explains 119.7% of the advantage and the selection is worth −£1,388.80** -- mildly value-destructive, the same sign on both windows. The £7,066 was a price rise wearing a model, and the seat that built the arm said so in the artefact instead of publishing the enterprise-value reading that said the opposite, correctly discarding it as R15 TAUTOLOGY because `build_enterprise_value` re-scores the book under the very belief the arm optimised against. **And the reason is not a defect in the company.** `WHAT_A_HOUSEHOLD_DECIDES_ON.md` audits the world and finds every axis is a UNIVERSAL RESPONSE FUNCTION while the three drawn per-household attitude axes -- `price_sensitivity`, `green_stance`, `channel_pref`, each drawn, coverage-tested, wall-guarded and leak-mutation-tested -- are consumed by nothing. Two households in identical circumstances behave identically, so there is no household TYPE to infer, and a perfect company model would converge on the oracle and still demonstrate nothing deserving the word skill. The director saw this before the machine did and reframed the work in his own words -- *"the world's richness sets the maximum skill the company can ever demonstrate. So the SIM leads and the company catches up"* -- and that is now the spine. The full-window ladder landed in the same stretch and reversed its own 2019 headline: `median_world_over_believed` 1.160 to **0.768** on 22 common decisions against 6, unmatched decisions 18 to **0**, rung zero reproducing the flat-rules control to the penny at £152,114.248823. Three of five previous focus items are finished and gone from this list. Two are not, and both failed the same way: **EP1 was named for the sixth time and its ledger row still reads `measured_at: 2026-08-26T11:46:22Z` at `run_git_commit: 8afa34ceb`, and EP13 was given the company half for the fifth time and delivered SIM-side work for the fifth time** -- and the grep that item asked for was already answered on disk, at `EP13_CARBON_INTENSITY_DISCOVER_FRAME.md:63,67`, in the document the item itself named. Both were named by maturity-map atom id, which only BIASES the ordinary draw; every item that landed this stretch and last was a kebab slug that becomes Lane 0. That is a defect in my dial and item four below is where I change it. Nothing went backwards, but the project traded a claim for a truth: the headline it could have published went from "+£7,066 from a per-customer model" to "+£8,455 from a price level", and that is the right trade. What is at risk right now is that **S1 -- the first change that can raise the world's ceiling -- is sitting UNCOMMITTED**: 127 lines across `simulation/market_switching_propensity.py`, `simulation/customer_events.py` and `simulation/population_draw.py`, in a working tree with three writers, with a test file beside it and a call-site comment asserting a mean-preservation its own sibling note has already measured false. Landing that is the first thing this direction owes.

focus.what: ADOPT the uncommitted S1 work already in the working tree -- do not rebuild it. `git status` shows `simulation/market_switching_propensity.py` (+76: `PRICE_SENSITIVITY_WEIGHT` high 1.5 / medium 1.0 / low 0.4, `price_sensitivity_weight`, `perceived_price_differential`), `simulation/customer_events.py` (+30: the call site inside `roll_lifecycle_event` that now feeds `churn_position_multiplier` the FELT differential), `simulation/population_draw.py` (+23: `price_sensitivity_for_customer`, delegating to the same `_draw_curriculum_axis` substream `assign_cohort` uses), and `tests/simulation/test_price_sensitivity_reaches_the_price_response.py`. If HEAD already carries it, skip straight to the re-grade. Three things to repair before landing. (a) The call-site comment in `customer_events.py` states the change is mean-preserving and that "the book's aggregate price response is unchanged and only its spread is new" -- the sibling note in `market_switching_propensity.py` measured that claim FALSE and says so: `churn_position_multiplier` is convex, so by Jensen the mean response RISES, `E[m(d*w)] / m(d)` reaching 1.142 at −20% and 1.118 at +20%. Correct the call-site comment to match the measured note; it is the one a reader of the churn decision actually sees. (b) `from simulation.live_population import _DEFAULT_BASE_SEED` is a private constant AND it pins the behaviour draw to the DEFAULT seed rather than the seed the run used -- which is precisely the cohort/behaviour disagreement `price_sensitivity_for_customer`'s own docstring says the single-mechanism design exists to prevent. Either thread the run's base seed to the decision point, or prove no live run varies it and say so in the docstring. (c) R15 both ways on the WIRING, not just the weighting: the mutation that must go red is the one that makes the weight a no-op (all three weights 1.0), because a weight that is drawn and then not felt is exactly the failure this change exists to remove. Then run `python3 -m tools.grade_renewal_churn_belief` at a commit carrying S1 and report, beside the pre-S1 figures: `oracle_ceiling.discrimination_auc` (was 0.8109), both graded AUCs (0.5586 and 0.5275), the three believed buckets, and `mechanism.attenuation_factor` (was 7.757). Change no constant in `saas/churn_model.py` -- R12, every figure there is a diagnostic.
focus.why: This is the director's own reframing turned into an act: the world's richness caps demonstrable skill, so the SIM leads. The oracle ceiling is the number that says how much inference is available and the graded AUCs say how little is captured, and S1 is the first change in the project's history that can move the ceiling rather than the capture. It goes first for a second reason that has nothing to do with its rank: 127 lines of load-bearing simulation change are sitting uncommitted in a tree with three concurrent writers, which is how this project has lost work before. Finished when the wiring is committed AND pushed with its controls green, the call-site comment no longer contradicts its own module's measurement, the seed question is answered one way or the other, and the belief grade has been re-run at a commit carrying S1 with the new ceiling stated beside 0.8109. If the ceiling does not move, that is a complete and valuable answer and it says the weighting is too small to matter -- report it, do not enlarge the weights to make it move.

focus.what: Run `python3 -m tools.couple_cohort` at HEAD and record the `price_sensitivity` leg's believed-vs-drawn gap as the PRE-S1 baseline, in the coupled ledger beside the other rows. Then answer one structural question in a design document, with the code open. The curriculum (`docs/design/segmentation_curriculum_v1.json`) declares `price_sensitivity` `hidden_truth_only: false` and names its channel: *"discoverable via rate-change churn response (get_churn_estimate)"*. That channel is implemented -- `company/analytics/cohort_discovery.py:177 _infer_price_sensitivity` bands the company's own `get_churn_estimate` output at 0.45 and 0.15 -- but the number it bands is `build_churn_risk` derived, i.e. the company's own BELIEF about the household, which the 478-renewal grade shows is bill-shock count re-labelled. A belief is not an observation of behaviour, so the channel plausibly cannot carry S1's new signal no matter how much of it the world produces. State whether it can, with the evidence; if it cannot, name the observable that could -- a real supplier observes each household's realised accept-or-leave outcome after its own rate change, which is a behaviour and not a model output -- and file that as the owed work. Do NOT edit `segmentation_curriculum_v1.json`: the marginals and its declared shares are the director's under R13; record the contract gap in the design doc instead.
focus.why: The thesis says the advantage must come from INFERENCE and never from ACCESS, so a household type the company cannot learn raises the world's ceiling and the company's gap at the same instant and will read as the company getting worse. This is the "company catches up" half of the director's steer, and it is cheap because the instrument already exists -- `tools/couple_cohort.py` grades the believed cohort against the drawn truth and its thresholds were set blind to the curriculum, which is the independence the gap needs to mean anything. Third because the pre-S1 baseline is only readable before S1 changes the world, so the RUN is genuinely urgent even though the analysis is not. Finished when the `price_sensitivity` gap has a pre-S1 number recorded and a document states plainly whether the declared discovery channel is capable of carrying the signal at all. "The channel reads the company's own belief and therefore cannot" is the more likely answer and is a complete one.

The level-vs-selection tool was built, run, and returned a 9.4x headline that was an artefact twice over, and it was withdrawn in the same turn before anything was published. Confound one: `decide_margin`'s FLAT branch returns before the `lawful` filter, so the counterfactual let one arm offer £39.50 above the cap while clamping the other. Confound two, and fatal to the approach: `renewal_margin_uplift` returns `MarginArmUplift(0.0)` for FLAT_RULES, so overriding `TARGET_MARGIN_GBP_PER_MWH` raised the base tariff of every contract rather than the 25 renewals the value arm priced. Recorded as an error rather than a save because several hours went into a route whose second confound was readable in the adapter's first three lines -- but the catch itself was the right move and took two minutes, made by asking what the number would have to mean for it to be true.

A 15.8% breach rate against the Ofgem cap was measured -- 28,093 of 178,229 domestic electricity settlement records above `get_cap_unit_rate_for_date` -- and was two minutes from being reported as a compliance finding. what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
